title: Time-Domain 3D Electromagnetic Fields Estimation Based on Physics-Informed Deep Learning Framework
problem: Electromagnetic simulation via FDTD is computationally expensive in RF/microwave circuit design. Current physics-informed learning and data-driven approaches have limitations in accuracy or speed.
motivation: Design iteration cycles require fast electromagnetic simulation; FDTD bottleneck limits design productivity in RF/microwave domains.
method: The approach trains a neural network to predict electromagnetic fields (how electricity and magnetism spread through space) while enforcing Maxwell's equations—the fundamental physics laws of electromagnetism—as constraints during training. Instead of using fixed weights to balance physics and data accuracy, the system automatically adjusts these weights at each training step, letting both objectives improve together. This avoids running expensive electromagnetic simulations (called FDTD), achieving over 200 times faster predictions than traditional methods.
key_novelty: The innovation is an algorithm that automatically adjusts the importance of physics constraints versus data accuracy during training, allowing both objectives to improve together.
contributions: Physics-informed loss functions for Maxwell's equations in deep learning
Self-adaptive loss scaling factors algorithm (8.4% better than ReLoBRaLo)
14% MSE reduction versus pure data-driven learning, 15% versus FNO

metrics.other: 14% MSE reduction vs data-driven, 15% vs FNO

limitations: Specific to time-domain 3D EM field estimation; applicability to other PDE domains and frequency-domain analysis unclear.
primary_theme: Physics-informed deep learning for rapid 3D electromagnetic field simulation
